skill.name: designing-and-implementing
skill.description: Guides feature work from requirements through design options, planning, task creation, and implementation using the bpsai-pair workflow.
skill.summary: Plan and implement multi-step coding work with structured design, tasks, and lifecycle commands.
skill.author: BPSAI

security_audit.summary: All 17 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences or inline backticks; no Ruby backtick execution exists. The skill does show shell commands that place raw user request text in double quotes, which can be unsafe if copied directly. No prompt injection text or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: User request text is shown inside double-quoted shell arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Pass request text through stdin or a structured CLI argument. If shell use is required, escape user text before running commands.

remediation.issue: The workflow relies on local bpsai-pair commands and Trello sync steps.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands require user approval and should run only in trusted repositories with the expected CLI installed.

semantic_findings.title: Raw User Text in Shell Command Examples
semantic_findings.description: The planning examples place a user request inside double-quoted shell arguments. If copied directly, shell substitution in a malicious request could execute before bpsai-pair receives it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples explicitly pass user request text through shell commands. The risk depends on direct copying into a shell, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Complex feature requests can drift without a clear plan. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through design, task planning, and implementation steps.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether a request needs planning with bpsai-pair intent commands.
Suggests a workflow for feature, refactor, or multi-step work.
Guides clarification of goals, affected components, and open questions.
Prompts comparison of two or three implementation approaches.
Defines plan and task creation steps for .paircoder files.
Connects task implementation with TDD and lifecycle management skills.
limitations: Requires the bpsai-pair CLI for command-based steps.
Does not implement code by itself without repository context.
Trello sync depends on configured project credentials and permissions.
Command examples need safe handling when user text contains shell characters.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a feature request into clarified requirements, design options, tasks, and implementation order.

use_cases.title: Structure a Refactor
use_cases.description: Compare approaches before changing shared code and create tasks with clear acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Project Work
use_cases.description: Create plan and task records, then sync ready work to Trello when configured.

prompt_templates.title: Decide If Planning Is Needed
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this request and tell me if it needs a design plan before coding: [request].

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Feature Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Restate the goal, identify affected components, and ask only the questions needed before design: [request].

prompt_templates.title: Compare Implementation Approaches
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose three approaches for this change, list pros and cons, and recommend one: [context and request].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Plan and Task Breakdown
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan with ordered tasks, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and safe command steps for this feature: [feature].

output_examples.input: User asks to add a saved reports feature.
output: A short restatement of the goal.
A list of affected areas such as storage, UI, and permissions.
Two or three design options with a recommendation.

output_examples.input: User asks for a broad refactor.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends planning first, compares approaches, and creates implementation tasks before code changes begin.

output_examples.input: User asks to fix a typo.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends skipping formal planning and handling the small change directly.

best_practices: Use this skill for changes that affect several files, systems, or decisions.
Confirm ambiguous requirements before creating tasks or running workflow commands.
Keep task acceptance criteria testable and linked to the user goal.
anti_patterns: Using the full flow for trivial edits that do not need planning.
Running command examples with unescaped user text or untrusted input.
Creating tasks before choosing an implementation approach.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for feature work, refactors, architecture choices, and multi-step implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with small fixes?
faq.answer: It can triage them, but it recommends skipping formal planning for typo fixes and small bugs.

faq.question: Does it require bpsai-pair?
faq.answer: The workflow references bpsai-pair commands, so command automation requires that CLI.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: It guides planning and task execution. Code changes still depend on repository context and the implementation agent.

faq.question: Can it sync to Trello?
faq.answer: Yes, the skill includes a Trello sync step when project integration is configured.

faq.question: Is it safe to run the command examples?
faq.answer: Run them only after review. Escape user-provided text or pass it through a safer interface.
